summary: Drivepast Phase 3 (design pass + Leaflet/OSM maps) tested end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_phase3_maps.py (10 tests) covering GET /api/map/fleet, GET /api/engine/options/{id}, unit timeline lat/lon, map-vs-timeline parity across all 6 vans, and is_new flag after accept->undo. Re-ran /app/backend/tests/test_drivepast_api.py (18) and /app/backend/tests/test_phase2_engine.py (18). Combined 46/46 pass. Playwright UI run verified JRN-44..52: Van 2 unit map (20 numbered markers + depot, polyline in #7C3AED, '© OpenStreetMap contributors' attribution, popup with name/address/arrival/window, drawn in ~4ms); Dispatch fleet-map (6 distinct colored polylines, 6 legend items, Van 5 click navigates to /units/van-5, drawn in ~9ms); Engine test 'Show on map' navigates to /units/van-2?preview=<id>, renders map-request-pin-0/1 with dashed paths and the 'Showing the proposed new stops (dashed line). Nothing is booked.' banner while leaving Van 2 at 20 stops; booked stops after /api/engine/accept show 22 markers with 2 is-new (markers 16 and 18 after re-sequencing), and /api/engine/undo restores 20 markers with 0 is-new; blocking tile.openstreetmap.org still draws lines+markers and shows 'Map tiles couldn't load. Routes are still shown.' via map-tiles-error; at 390x844 Page tab, document scrollWidth equals clientWidth (no horizontal scroll) and the map fits width (358px with 16px gutters). Demo data was reset at the start and end.

issues: JRN-49 copy says 'markers 21/22 are New' but the engine inserts the new pickup/dropoff mid-route, so after re-sequencing the New markers end up at mid-route seqs (observed 16 and 18) rather than 21/22. REQ-166 only requires markers to match timeline position (verified) so behavior is correct, but the journey copy is misleading.

critical_code_review_comments: RouteMap.jsx tile failure detection fires only if `failed>=2 && loaded===0`. Any single successful tile anywhere in the viewport will prevent the error banner even if 90% of tiles fail; this is still spec-compliant (REQ-177 is 'if tiles fail to load') but a stricter ratio-based threshold would be more honest.

RouteMap.jsx re-creates the entire Leaflet map on every `routes`/`proposal` change (useEffect depends on both). For single-unit page this is fine, but updating a proposal re-paints the whole route; could be optimized with a layer group diff.
RouteMap.jsx uses an inline <div> popup string with manual HTML escape helper `esc`. OK, but consider React-leaflet Popup if more content is added later.
engine_api.map_fleet calls today_plans + unit_stops in a loop per unit without parallelism; harmless at 6 units but easy to parallelize with asyncio.gather.

RouteMap.jsx uses `dragging: !L.Browser.mobile` which disables dragging on desktop touch devices (Chrome on a Surface, iPads in desktop mode). Consider using `L.Browser.touch` only to toggle `touchZoom` and keep dragging always on.
